rv.q: In its strongest moments, the adaptation captures the riptide sensation of being pulled far from safe shores.
What is moving here, even in a murky production with too much stillness at its center, is the assembled talents
It glides by smoothly, and Ms. Mann's lilting, melancholy songs are hypnotically lovely, but the characters' anguish and psychological distress are only faintly sketched in.
Like its predecessors in print and onscreen, ultimately this latest rendition of Girl, Interrupted raises more questions than it answers.
Girl, Interrupted is elegant, often engaging theater. But it lilts through its world rather than diving into it.
Fans of Mann and Marjok, as well as theatergoers truly interested in viewing fresh, vital, new works of music drama should try to get a ticket to this compelling production.
Majok can't entirely crack the problem of turning a one-voiced memoir into a richly multi-voiced piece–but Mann's songs buoy her efforts, making the whole thing richer, sadder, fuller.

The show is more compelling when it begins to look at other characters besides Susanna, and how they deal with the pressures of the outside world—or don’t. Still, Majok tries to thread the needle between recapturing the interiority and fragmentary storytelling of the memoir and the Hollywoodized drama of the film with uneven results.
However, it falls short of developing the characters into people the audience can really feel for.
There's plenty of beautiful, delicate, heartfelt work in the mix. But whatever the blend of complicating pathologies, this girl still feels fettered.
Girl, Interrupted still really needs more time in development to be completely effective.

One in particular, “Girl Interrupted at Her Music” was particularly haunting. As with most of Vermeer’s paintings, the scenes invite the viewer to complete the narrative as they experience it—a kind of fine art Rorschach test, if you will. In this painting, a man stands over a woman, dominating her with his presence as she looks out at the viewer.
Girl, Interrupted celebrates the strength in sisterhood, the power of music and storytelling to find meaning in the darkest episodes of human experience.
Girl, Interrupted has an amazing score to balm even the most hardened of souls.
Girl, Interrupted is doing something genuinely difficult: rendering the texture of a disordered memory with theatrical and musical honesty, without sentimentality and without exploitation.
Atmospherically rich and thematically urgent, Girl, Interrupted is held back by a script that observes more than it inhabits.

cn.t: Critics praise this achingly beautiful musical adaptation of Susanna Kaysen's memoir, highlighting Martyna Majok and Aimee Mann's striking songs, crackling dialogue, and abiding sensitivity in capturing the disorienting experience of mental illness.
